prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. Captains complained that unloading at his port took twice as long as at the larger ports on the river. His reports note differences between the crates and the ships' papers as small as a bolt of cloth a yard short, and when his successor checked twenty years of them against the shippers' own invoices, he found them accurate to the last item. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: Slow unloading, tiny discrepancies recorded, and reports later found exact to the last item together show he was "meticulous." "Naive" fails because he checked the crates against the ships' papers rather than accepting them; "lenient" fails because the passage reports how closely he checked, not how mildly he punished; "incorruptible" fails because nothing concerns bribes or attempts to sway him.

naive.quote: differences between the crates and the ships' papers
naive.why: he compared goods with declarations rather than taking them on trust

lenient.quote: as small as a bolt of cloth a yard short
lenient.why: the passage is about the thoroughness of his checking, not about mild treatment of offenders

incorruptible.why: his distinction is precision; no one is said to have tried to buy him

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. His reports show him finding smuggled tobacco or brandy in the crates about as often as the inspectors at the larger ports on the river. Captains caught at those ports paid the full penalty the law set. Captains caught at his port usually paid only the duty they had tried to avoid, and many of them were caught there again. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He detected smuggling as often as other inspectors but let offenders off with only the duty owed, so he was "lenient." "Naive" fails because he found smuggled goods at the normal rate and so was not being fooled; "meticulous" fails because his detection rate was merely ordinary; "incorruptible" fails because the passage concerns his penalties, not any refusal of bribes.

naive.why: he regularly uncovered smuggled goods, so he was not being taken in

meticulous.quote: about as often as the inspectors
meticulous.why: an ordinary detection rate, no better than other ports, shows ordinary care, not exceptional precision

incorruptible.quote: paid only the duty they had tried to avoid
incorruptible.why: what distinguishes him is mild penalties, not resistance to bribery

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. He took each captain's word for what the crates held, and smugglers soon learned to mark crates of brandy as machine parts and crates of tobacco as books. On the rare days a crate split open on the quay, he fined its captain the full amount the law allowed and wrote in his report that he could not imagine how such a thing had happened. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: He believed what captains told him, smugglers exploited that trust with false labels, and even caught red-handed he could not see how it was done, so he was "naive." "Lenient" fails because when he did catch a captain he imposed the full fine; "meticulous" fails because he did not check the crates against their labels; "incorruptible" fails because smugglers did not need to buy him: they simply deceived him.

lenient.quote: the full amount the law allowed
lenient.why: he punished to the limit when he caught anyone, the reverse of mild treatment

meticulous.why: he accepted declarations instead of examining the goods

incorruptible.quote: mark crates of brandy as machine parts
incorruptible.why: the smugglers got through by deception, so his honesty toward bribes is never at issue

worlds.passage: From 1878 to 1901 a single inspector examined the cargo landed at a small river port for the customs service. Merchants' letters show that gifts of wine and banknotes eased crates through the other ports on the river. The same letters show such gifts to his port stopping within a year of his arrival, soon after two captains who had sent them were prosecuted on his reports. Reading his reports a century later, one historian described the inspector as ______.
worlds.explanation: Gifts that bought easy passage elsewhere stopped at his port once captains who sent them were prosecuted on his evidence, so he was "incorruptible." "Lenient" fails because he turned the givers over for prosecution; "naive" fails because he recognized the gifts for what they were; "meticulous" fails because the passage concerns how he answered bribes, not how thoroughly he inspected cargo.

lenient.why: he had offenders prosecuted, the reverse of letting them off lightly

naive.why: merchants stopped because he saw the gifts as bribes and acted on it

meticulous.quote: eased crates through the other ports
meticulous.why: what sets him apart from other ports is his refusal of payment, not careful counting
